extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and IP professionals analyzing industrial design statistics and procedural performance
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting WIPO industrial design statistical and procedural metrics (registrations, applications, examination outcomes, pendency, examiners, origin breakdowns) and their methodological notes for cross-office comparison and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of industrial design registrations in force at an office (note: refers to number of registrations in force and not the number of designs contained in those registrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: WIPO Statistics Database. Use this count as the office-level stock of active design registrations; do not confuse with the number of designs contained within multi-design registrations. Examples in tables list registrations in force by office (e.g., EUIPO, China, US).

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth rate (%) of registrations/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-on-year percentage change (growth rate) for registrations or applications reported for offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts and tables present growth rates (e.g., +24.1%, –17.2%). Interpret in context of base volumes and possible missing data for some offices; large percentage changes can be driven by changes in reporting or one-off effects (e.g., UK spike in 2022 due to EU exit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force as percentage of total registrations (by registration year)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a given registration year t, the percentage of designs registered in year t that remain in force in 2023, calculated as (number registered in year t and in force in 2023) / (total number registered in year t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure note: percentages are calculated using the number of industrial designs registered in year t and in force in 2023 divided by the total number of industrial designs registered in year t. The graph is based on data from 81 offices for which breakdowns were available. China is excluded from the figure because its differing protection term (10 years) and large share would distort the global pattern. Industrial design rights generally last up to 15 years from filing (China: 10 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of industrial design registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of years since registration for industrial design registrations that were in force at a given date (e.g., average age at selected offices in 2018 and 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an average (years) by office. Use to assess the maturity/turnover of the in-force stock. Comparisons across offices should consider differing rights durations and reporting coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of examination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Share (percentage) of applications by examination outcome categories: Registered, Rejected, Withdrawn/abandoned (for selected offices, e.g., 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as stacked-bar distributions by office. WIPO collects data via a common questionnaire but procedural differences between offices mean outcomes are not fully harmonized—exercise caution when comparing outcome shares across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially pending applications (by office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of applications that are potentially pending at an office (reported for selected offices, e.g., 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables list potentially pending application counts for offices. Note that data for some large offices are missing (e.g., China, Italy, Japan), so totals and comparisons may be incomplete; methodological notes warn of incomplete reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average pendency times (days) — first office action and final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Average elapsed days from filing date to first office action and from filing date to final office decision at selected offices (reported separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency is shown in days for first office action and final decision. Because offices have different procedural practices and reporting definitions, WIPO cautions that these pendency figures cannot be fully harmonized; exercise caution comparing across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of industrial design examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiners expressed in full time equivalent (FTE) engaged in industrial design examination at an office (reported by office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: FTE is full time equivalent. Use to assess resourcing relative to application volumes and pendency. Differences in what offices report as examiners or how they allocate FTE may limit comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design count by office and origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Application design count broken down by office: Total, Resident, Non-resident, Change over previous year; and by origin (resident vs abroad equivalent design count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present application design counts for every office with resident/non-resident split and year-over-year changes. Footnotes: design count by origin data are incomplete because some offices do not report the relevant data. An application filed at a regional office is considered resident if the applicant resides in one of that office’s member states. Codes: n.a. = not applicable; .. = not available. (b) Hague-designation-only data and other footnotes mean origin data may be incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration design count by office and origin, and registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration design count by office (Total, Resident, Non-resident) and equivalent registration design count by origin; plus registrations in force by office and change over previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar structure to application counts but for registrations and in-force stocks. Footnotes indicate incomplete origin reporting for some offices, Hague-only data, and special handling for regional/processing offices (e.g., Benelux, OAPI). Use caution when summing or comparing across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design office procedural data (processed outcomes and backlogs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each office: total applications processed, counts registered, rejected, withdrawn/abandoned, applications pending, number of examiners (FTE), first office action (days), final office decision (days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a comprehensive procedural table by office. WIPO notes that despite a common questionnaire, procedural differences and omissions may make cross-office harmonization difficult; totals for an office may be incomplete if elements are omitted by the office. (a) indicates data for formalities examinations only for some offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness, footnotes and special-code meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnote and notation rules used throughout the tables: n.a. indicates not applicable; .. indicates not available; (a),(b),(c),(d) indicate specific caveats such as Hague-only data, regional office processing, or incomplete origin reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult footnotes on each table: e.g., (a) Hague designation data only and/or office not reporting origin; (c) OAPI is competent office for processing applications; (d) Benelux Office is competent office for processing applications. These annotations affect interpretation of resident/non-resident splits and completeness of counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological harmonization caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from offices using a common questionnaire and methodology but differences in industrial design procedures between offices mean data cannot be fully harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated caution across figure and table notes: 'Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.' Users should not directly equate figures across offices without accounting for differences in definitions, coverage, and reporting practices; use metadata and footnotes to adjust comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/identifier notes (e.g., EUIPO, FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided for identifiers used in tables: e.g., 'EUIPO is the European Union Intellectual Property Office.' 'FTE is full time equivalent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions when interpreting table headings and units. They clarify organizational acronyms and measurement units used in the report.
